title: The Underworld after the Armistice
summary: The dead from November 1918 to the eve of the 1929 crash.

claims.text: The setting covers the years from Armistice Day, 11 November 1918, up to the night before the stock market crash of 1929.
Charon still rules the Empire in theory, though no one has seen Charon in years.
Stygia has fallen to treachery, and the Dark Kingdom of Iron is close to collapse.
The Shadowlands are all but cut off from the Empire's heart, and every Necropolis stands alone among enemies.

title: The Fourth Great Maelstrom
summary: The psychic storm born of the Somme.

claims.text: The carnage of the Somme spawned the Fourth Great Maelstrom, which still rages.
The storm lasts until the Shadow-eaten who make it up are beaten and the Nihils sealed.
A Maelstrom is a violent venting from the Tempest or Labyrinth into the Shadowlands, usually with Spectres.

title: The War of the Dead
summary: What wraiths mean by the Great War.

claims.text: Among wraiths the Great War means the Underworld conflict that follows the living one; the living war they call the War to End All Wars, or just the war.
Ghosts of tanks, zeppelins and planes, drones re-running doomed charges and drifting clouds of poison gas fill the Underworld.

title: The Insurrection
summary: The Grim Legion's grab for the Dark Empire.

claims.text: The Insurrection is the Grim Legion's attempt to take the Dark Empire of Iron.
Its supporters call themselves Imperialists of the New Stygian regime; opponents call them Insurrectionists.
A Loyalist is a wraith who fights against the Smiling Lord's side in the Insurrection.
Grim Legion traitors may already be inside a Citadel's walls.

title: Black Mask and the Ministry of Intelligence
summary: The spy services of the Legions.

claims.text: The Black Mask is the Grim Legion's espionage order.
The Ministry of Intelligence is the Iron Legion's espionage order.
The Magisterium Veritatis is Stygia's secret police.

title: Orders of the Legions
summary: Some named orders and branches of the 1920s Legions.

claims.text: The Bleak Legion is not a real Legion at all but a Russian offshoot of the Silent Legion.
The Cataphractoi serve the Legion of Fate as its heavy cavalry.
The Penitent Legion's Flesh Corps fights with moliated Leviathans, as the Beast Corps uses barghests.

title: The Breathless Dead
summary: Stygia's name for the dead of the Spanish Flu.

claims.text: Stygians call victims of the Spanish Flu the Breathless Dead.

title: Other Deadlands
summary: The afterlives beyond Stygia drawn into the war.

claims.text: The age also sweeps up the souls of the Jade Empire, of the Bush of Ghosts and of the Indian afterlife.
The Bush of Ghosts is the African Deadlands, called the Dark Kingdom of Ivory in Stygia.
The Jade Kingdom is the Asian Deadlands; Yellow Springs is its term for China's Deadlands.
Some travellers brave the Maelstrom to go home, or find themselves captive in afterlives not their own.

title: Words of the Far Deadlands
summary: Terms from the Jade Kingdom, the Bush of Ghosts and Swar.

claims.text: In the Jade Kingdom, hun is the intellect and spirit, the Psyche, which makes up half of a wraith's soul; a kuei is a malevolent spirit ruled by its p'o.
In the Bush of Ghosts an ibambo is an African wraith, and a moriman is a spirit doctor who practises the Behest Arcanos.
Stygians call the Arcanos practised by the Tvashtriya Displace.
Yama is held to be lord of the Dead and judge of souls in the Indian afterlife.

title: Generals of Oblivion
summary: Nephwracks in Oblivion's direct service.

claims.text: The Generals of Oblivion are a small band of Nephwracks who answer to Oblivion itself and side with or against Malfeans as they please.
The Mutile is a common Spectre, called a Mortwight in the European Deadlands.

title: Johnny Songbirds
summary: Wandering Chanteurs of the age.

claims.text: Johnny Songbirds are itinerant Chanteurs.

title: The Night of Short Chains
summary: The coup that unseated the Deathlord of Madness.

claims.text: During the Night of Short Chains, 250 Grim Guards back the Smiling Lord as the Laughing Lady is made to abdicate.
Black Mask agents open the postern gate of the Seat of Succor, and the abdicated Deathlord is replaced by a Laughing Lady of the Grim Lord's choosing.

title: The Penitent Legion
summary: Keepers of those lost to madness.

claims.text: The Legion takes in those who die of madness, their own or another's; it is small but politically ambitious.
The rightful Laughing Lady escapes into exile while the new one holds the mask of office, splitting the Legion between Imperialists and Loyalists.
It holds insanity to be Oblivion showing itself, watches its mad members closely through the Keepers, and spends much effort on the Shadow and on fighting Spectres.

title: The Skeletal Legion
summary: The Legion of the diseased.

claims.text: Of the three great Deathlords, the Skeletal Lord is held to be the most dangerous.
The Legion is highly efficient and grows all through the war, yet the flood of new dead still overwhelms it.
Influenza dead pour into its ranks, reaped by its functionaries.

title: The Emerald Legion
summary: The most conservative of the Legions.

claims.text: Its Anacreons work as tax farmers, and its regular army is perhaps the weakest of any Legion.
It first backs the Smiling Lord, expecting the coup to win, then abandons that cause and joins the Loyalists.

title: The Iron Battalions
summary: The Iron Legion's main fighting force.

claims.text: The Iron Battalions are the Iron Legion's premier troops, matched perhaps only by the Unlidded Eye's soldiers and the Cataphractoi who serve Fate.
Grim Legion success in turning key figures in the Iron Legion's spy network causes the Iron Legion heavy early losses.

title: The Legion of Fate
summary: The Lady of Fate's own Legion.

claims.text: Above all the Legion serves the Lady of Fate, who is usually taken to want what is best for the whole Underworld.
The Lady's seat, a vast mansion, stands on the Isle of Eurydice out in the Tempest, given by Charon in thanks for help during that reign.

title: The Silent Legion
summary: The Legion of those who chose death.

claims.text: The Silent Legion is made up of individualists who chose their own way into the Underworld and bear that final free choice as their mark.
It supplies many Pardoners, Oracles and volunteers for the Magisterium.
The Warriors of Lethe are an elite unit of members who wish to end their existence but want to strike at Oblivion first.

title: The Beggar Lord
summary: Deathlord of the Paupers.

claims.text: No neutral in the Insurrection is paid better than the Beggar Lord.
Everyone in the Legion of Revelations spies for the Beggar Lord at some level, with strong networks in the Jade and Ivory Dark Kingdoms.
The Beggar Lord forbids those troops from entering the Labyrinth, so their knowledge of it is poor.
Those who die of old age serve in the Legion of Paupers.

title: How Death Picks a Legion
summary: The manner of death sets the Legion.

claims.text: Those taken by disease join the Skeletal Legion, the old serve the Beggar Lord among the Paupers, and victims of Despair or Madness join the Silent or Penitent Legion.
Influenza was the deadliest killer of the period.

title: Trials under the Grim Legion
summary: Justice for the war dead.

claims.text: Grim Legion Advocates try not only wraiths who murdered in life but those indirectly to blame, chiefly senior officers.
Judges and juries favour the Grim Legion, so countless officers and leaders are branded killers and go to the forges after hasty hearings.

title: The Monitors' Bargain
summary: The Grim Legion's deal with extortionists.

claims.text: Before the rebellion the Grim Legion trades free rein under its rule for help from the Seven Families of the Monitors Guild.
The deal pays off for the Grim Legion but ruins the Seven Families, who clash badly with the Loyalists of the Spooks' Guild.

title: Stygian Trusts
summary: Money behind both sides.

claims.text: The Stygian Trusts fund both sides in the Grim Legion's rebellion, as they did in an earlier revolt.

title: Airships of the Dead
summary: Flying craft of the Legions.

claims.text: Airships serve as couriers and troop carriers for the Emerald Legion, the Victims of Mystery and the Legion of Fate.

title: Doppelgangers
summary: Spectres hidden among the Restless.

claims.text: Thousands of Doppelgangers work in the Twilight Era, burrowing into every level of society; some spy for the Generals of Oblivion.

title: Barcelona
summary: A Necropolis that fell without a fight.

claims.text: The Grim Legion takes Barcelona almost without a struggle and holds it more tightly than anywhere else.
